# Muto Runtime: Runtime Hot-Swap Library for Fabric Mods

> Author: fy2ne (@fy2ne)
> Architecture: Runtime Knot Classpath Injection & MappedRegistry Thawing
> Type: Developer Library (client-side engine)
> Target: Minecraft Java Edition | Fabric Loader | Java 25+
> Package: me.fy2ne.muto (Maven group me.fy2ne, artifact muto)
> Website: https://muto.fy2ne.me
> Modrinth: https://modrinth.com/project/muto
> Repository: https://github.com/fy2ne/muto

## What Muto Runtime Is

Muto Runtime is a **developer library** - not a player-facing mod. It provides the JVM-level runtime primitives that make it possible to load, unload, and hot-swap Fabric mods while Minecraft is running, with no restart.

Players do not interact with Muto Runtime directly. They install mods that depend on it. Muto Runtime runs silently and does not add any UI to Minecraft itself.

## How It Works

Muto chains three runtime techniques:

1. **Knot Classpath Injection** - a newly added or updated mod jar is appended to Fabric Loader's running Knot classpath (with nested jars), so its classes resolve without a restart.

2. **Registry Thawing** - Minecraft freezes MappedRegistry at boot. Muto clears the frozen flag via a Mixin accessor (reflective fallback), prunes entries for the removed/updated mod's namespace, lets the new version re-register, then refreezes.

3. **Dynamic Mixin Registration** - the new jar's mixin configurations are registered with the global Mixin service and apply to every class the JVM defines after the reload. Mixin only weaves at class-definition time, so classes that are already loaded cannot be re-woven and cannot be reloaded without a restart.

## Integration

External mods declare Muto as an optional soft-dependency using `modCompileOnly`.

### Gradle

```groovy
repositories {
    maven {
        name = "Modrinth"
        url = "https://api.modrinth.com/maven"
    }
}
dependencies {
    modCompileOnly "maven.modrinth:muto:0.3.0-beta"
}
```

### Runtime Detection and Reload

```java
import net.fabricmc.loader.api.FabricLoader;
import me.fy2ne.muto.api.MutoApi;

public class DownloaderIntegration {
    public static void onModDownloaded(java.nio.file.Path jarPath) {
        if (!FabricLoader.getInstance().isModLoaded("muto")) return;

        if (MutoApi.isSafeToReload()) {
            MutoApi.reloadAsync().thenAccept(result -> {
                if (result.success()) {
                    System.out.println("hot-swapped in " + result.durationMs() + "ms");
                } else {
                    System.err.println("swap failed: " + result.error());
                }
            });
        }
    }
}
```

### Lifecycle Event Hooks

```java
import me.fy2ne.muto.api.MutoEvents;

MutoEvents.RELOAD_START.register((startMs, diff) -> {
    // close stale connections, clear texture caches
});

MutoEvents.RELOAD_FINISH.register((endMs, diff, success, durationMs, error) -> {
    // refresh caches, re-bind resources
});
```

## Public API

- `MutoApi.isAvailable()`: boolean - Muto is loaded and ready
- `MutoApi.isReloading()`: boolean - reload transaction is currently running
- `MutoApi.isSafeToReload()`: boolean - client is on title screen, not in a world
- `MutoApi.plan()`: ReloadPlan - scan /mods and compute a diff without executing
- `MutoApi.reloadAsync()`: CompletableFuture<ReloadResult> - trigger async hot-swap
- `MutoApi.reloadAsync(Consumer<String>)`: with per-stage progress callback
- `MutoApi.getReloadableModIds()`: Set<String> - all dynamically reloadable mods
- `MutoApi.getStubbornModIds()`: Set<String> - core mods that require a restart
- `MutoApi.startFileWatcher()`: boolean - start opt-in muto.trigger file watcher
- `MutoApi.stopFileWatcher()`: boolean - stop the watcher

## Mod Tier Classification

Muto classifies all mods at startup into three tiers:

- **Tier 1 (Clean)**: Pure client mods - HUDs, UI tweaks, visual mods. Reloads instantly with no registry involvement.
- **Tier 2 (Standard)**: Content mods - blocks, items, recipes, dimensions. Full pipeline: Knot injection, registry thaw, re-run ModInitializer, refreeze.
- **Tier 3 (Stubborn)**: Fabric Loader, Fabric API, core mixin injectors. Permanently locked in the root classloader. Cannot be reloaded without a JVM restart.

## Building and Testing

- Build: `./gradlew build` (compile, test, assemble). Jar: `./gradlew jar`. Dev client: `./gradlew runClient`.
- Fast-refresh loop: `./gradlew mutoWatch` (see `muto-watcher.gradle`).
- Tests: JUnit 5 - `junit-jupiter-api` 5.11.4, `junit-jupiter-engine` 5.11.4 and `junit-platform-launcher` 1.11.4, wired into the Loom `test` source set. Run `./gradlew test`; HTML report at `build/reports/tests/test/index.html`.
- Test classes: `ModStateManagerTest`, `ModTierClassificationTest`, `ReloadShellTest`, `api.MutoApiTest`.
- CI: `.github/workflows/build.yml` (Temurin JDK 25, `./gradlew build`) and `.github/workflows/publish.yml` (GitHub Packages).

## Source Layout

- `src/main/java/me/fy2ne/muto/api` - public surface (`MutoApi`, `MutoEvents`, `ModDiff`)
- `src/main/java/me/fy2ne/muto/engine` - `ReloadEngine`, `ModScanner`, `ModSnapshot`, `RegistryFreezer`, `MutoClassLoader`
- `src/main/java/me/fy2ne/muto/engine/knot` - Knot classpath injection and reflection access
- `src/main/java/me/fy2ne/muto/engine/mixin` - dynamic mixin registration
- `src/main/java/me/fy2ne/muto/mixin` - accessors and injections against Minecraft internals
- `src/main/java/me/fy2ne/muto/mods` - disk mod state and disabled-mods registry
- `src/main/java/me/fy2ne/muto/config` - `MutoConfig` (config/muto.json)

## Platform

- Minecraft: Java Edition 26.x (26.1, 26.1.1, 26.1.2, 26.2, 26.3)
- Loader: Fabric Loader >= 0.16.0
- Fabric API: >= 0.144.1
- Java: 25+
- Environment: Client-side only
- License: GNU Lesser General Public License v3.0 (LGPL-3.0-only) - Copyright 2026 fy2ne. Free to use and link from any mod, including closed-source ones; modifications to Muto itself must remain open under the LGPL. https://www.gnu.org/licenses/lgpl-3.0.html

A JDK with class-redefinition support (JBR/DCEVM) is not required; Muto reloads by injecting jars into Knot and re-running initializers.
